about: Which command to run for what you want to check. README.md renders this file between its chooser markers with scripts/chooser.mjs; edit it here, then run node scripts/chooser.mjs --write. An example runs its command in a copy of a committed fixture and declares the exit code, and a nextExample does the same for the next command. An example whose command has the operand - names the fixture file it reads on standard input in stdin. scripts/chooser-captures.mjs --write records the output in the capture file and how it was made in the sidecar beside it.
question: What do you want to check?

options.ask: My own project, before I ship it
options.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a critical or high finding to fix before you ship.

options.ask: A package, repository or skill, before I install it
options.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a high or critical risk.

options.ask: A running agent endpoint you own
options.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a payload that succeeded; exit 2 means nothing answered.

options.ask: One text, such as a pull request body
options.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a high or critical line that overrides instructions or claims authority.

options.ask: Every agent project under this folder
options.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a high or critical finding in one of them.

more.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a critical control not detected.

more.ask: Attack payloads to run yourself against a skill, MCP config or SOUL.md
more.findingMeans: It does not run them, so it does not tell you whether the artifact resists.

more.ask: MCP endpoints a host you own exposes
more.findingMeans: Exit 1 is a critical or high exposure.
